scholarships.title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
scholarships.official_source: U.S. Department of State (Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs)

existing.description: The Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program is a U.S. Department of State fellowship, administered by the Institute of International Education, for mid-career professionals from eligible countries. It is a non-degree program: fellows may take academic coursework at a U.S. host university but do not earn a degree. The package covers host-university tuition and fees, a maintenance allowance with a one-time settling-in allowance, accident and sickness insurance, a book allowance, a one-time computer subsidy, international and programme-event air travel, and a professional development allowance. Applications go through each applicant's Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section, so deadlines vary by country and nominations must reach IIE by mid-September.
eligibility: Accomplished mid-level professional from a designated Humphrey country.
Typically 5 or more years of professional experience.
Demonstrated leadership potential and commitment to public service.
Must be nominated by the U.S. Embassy or Binational Fulbright Commission in home country.
English proficiency sufficient for graduate-level study in the U.S.
existing.eligibility_summary: Accomplished mid-level professionals from designated countries; typically 5+ years of professional experience; bachelor's degree; demonstrated leadership and commitment to public service; must be nominated by U.S. Embassy or Fulbright Commission in home country.
benefits: Tuition and fees at host university
Monthly living/maintenance allowance (includes one-time settling-in allowance)
coverage: Tuition and fees at host university
Monthly living/maintenance allowance (includes one-time settling-in allowance)
requirements: Apply through the Binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section in your country rather than directly to the programme
Submit complete answers to all questions with English essay responses addressing the prompt
Submit two English recommendation letters, one from the current employer
documents: Online application via U.S. Embassy or Fulbright Commission
Two letters of recommendation (one from current employer)
existing.english_requirement: English proficiency sufficient for graduate-level study; demonstrated through application essays, recommendations, and transcripts. No specific test score minimum centrally required, but host university may require TOEFL/IELTS.
application_method: Apply through U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section or Binational Fulbright Commission in home country
existing.selection_notes: After national selection, independent review committees in the United States review the nominations, and final candidate approval is determined by the J. William Fulbright Foreign Scholarship Board. Fellows are assigned in groups of 13-15 to one of the host institutions best matched to their professional field; they cannot choose their university.
existing.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from designated countries seeking non-degree professional enrichment and graduate-level study in the U.S.
existing.notes: 10-month non-degree fellowship; not a degree program. Fellows are placed at selected U.S. universities. Awards announced in spring for fall start. Cannot combine with other U.S. government exchange programs.
existing.duration: Ten-month fellowship year (one academic year of study plus a pre-academic English and professional program), plus a six-week Professional Affiliation
existing.application_period: Varies by country; nominations due mid-September, fellowships begin August-September
existing.deadline_display: Varies by country — U.S. Embassies/Fulbright Commissions must submit nominations by mid-September
existing.program_type: Non-degree professional fellowship for mid-career professionals
